pr_title: Fix `PopupMenu` loops over items when `ui_down`/`ui_up` is pressed

issue_context.title: `PopupMenu` loops over items when the ui_down/ui_up button is pressed
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

4.2.2

### System information

win 10

### Issue description

after being visible in multi window mode (including editor), pressing the ui_down/ui_up loops over many items, because internal process is active when it becomes visible in multi window mode.

### Steps to reproduce

Press any main menu button in the editor and then press the ui_down/ui_up button.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
comments:
because the internal process is used to simulate gamepad echo event when we hold up/down buttons, but it can't check if it's a gamepad or keyboard keys, so it simulates the echo event rapidly when a key is just pressed at first time, resulting in looping over 3 or 4 menu items so fast when we just press the down or up keys. you can reveal any editor top menu with mouse and you press up or down keys once, you will notice it looping so fast over so many items. also the internal process is used to check if mouse enters the auto hide areas when using multible windows mode, so when the menu is visible in multible windows mode the internal process works and when the down/up keys is presseded the loop happens immediately while it was just intended to use the internal process for autohide areas not to simulate a gamepad echo when a keyboard key is pressed.<s> and to make it more confusing, the internal process will be disabled once a gamepad up/down key is released, so the autohide areas code will not work after that, so we need to disable the internal process only when the window is embedded.</s>

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/53877170/5b0eb8d9-8b4d-4a5a-aeb2-e45ed9296e32)

Fixed: we should disable the internal process under a condition here.
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/53877170/5c0e911b-452b-4a90-9899-c01ece9e4874)

for this code to work as expected.
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/53877170/4d5693ed-1c80-4a20-959b-e34c0fe6356a)

review_comments: "joypad" is how it's named in the API, I don't think this local variable rename is useful.
Nevermind, I see other code was already using "gamepad_event" here and you made this a member, so I agree with that name for local consistency.
